text:
Columbus arrives in Raleigh for game two of a three-game road trip, riding overtime wins in three of its last five. Kent Johnson won it in overtime at PHI on Tuesday, a 4-3 result in which the Blue Jackets held just 34% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality). Carolina, 3-1-1 over its last five, beat BOS 2-1 on Tuesday and has out-chanced every opponent in that stretch, but it is without Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal. Mark Jankowski is up to 17:16 a night from 14:10 since Hall went out, and Jackson Blake took Staal's spot beside Martinook and Ehlers.

The gap in play is wide. At five on five, Carolina has taken 60% of the expected goals to Columbus's 46%, and our model expects 3.5 goals for the Hurricanes tonight against 2.53 for the Blue Jackets. The Hurricanes also have the stronger power play (0.94 expected goals a game to 0.56) and penalty kill, though they take 4.1 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Pyotr Kochetkov is 5.5 goals saved above expected this season, while Jet Greaves sits at -0.5, though Greaves was at +15.0 over 55 games last year.

Sebastian Aho leads our scoring picks at 36% to score and 74% for a point. Logan Stankoven, one goal from 50 in his career, is at 30%. For Columbus, Johnson has 10 points in his last ten, though we'd say finishing is doing most of the work. Our under-the-radar pick is Jankowski, whose recent shots have been dangerous (3.2 expected goals in his last 10 games), and we have him at 22% to score.
